prompt: A structure is relaxed when what is small?

options.why: The force is the slope of the energy, so flat means no push left.
Tempting, but the energy changes very little near a minimum even while forces are still large.
Tempting, but the volume says nothing about whether the atoms still feel forces.

hints: Think of balls on a hilly landscape.
Which quantity is the slope?

prompt: Which unit does VASP use for forces in OUTCAR?

options.why: The TOTAL-FORCE block is given in eV per angstrom.
Tempting, but that is an energy, not a force.
Tempting, but VASP uses eV and angstrom here, not atomic units.

hints: A force is an energy divided by a length.
Look at the header of the TOTAL-FORCE block.

prompt: Why should every calculation you compare use the same OUTCAR energy line?

options.text: The entropy term depends on the smearing, so mixed lines add a numerical difference
options.why: Free energy and the sigma-to-0 energy differ by an entropy term that changes with SIGMA.
Tempting, but they all use eV; the difference is an entropy term.

options.text: Only one line is ever written
options.why: Tempting, but OUTCAR holds several energy lines in each ionic step.

hints: What does the free energy include that the other line does not?
Does the extra term depend on SIGMA?

prompt: Which readings suggest the forces of a step are unreliable?

options.why: VASP continues anyway, so the forces from that step are unreliable.
A large drift shows the forces are not consistent, often from loose convergence.

options.text: The step is the last one
options.why: Tempting, but being last says nothing about the quality of the forces.

hints: Think about electronic convergence.
What does the drift line check?

prompt: A very tight force criterion such as EDIFFG = -0.001 needs what else?

options.text: A tight EDIFF, such as 1E-7 or smaller
options.why: Forces are only as accurate as the SCF behind them.
Tempting, but a lower cutoff makes forces less accurate, not more.
Tempting, but a larger smearing does not make forces more accurate.

hints: Forces come from the electronic loop.
Which tag sets how tightly it converges?

prompt: How does VASP signal that a relaxation with a negative EDIFFG reached its criterion?

options.text: It prints reached required accuracy in OUTCAR
options.why: That line appears when every force is below the absolute value of EDIFFG.
Tempting, but a job also ends when it runs out of steps (NSW).
Tempting, but a flat energy can hide forces that are still large.

hints: Look for a phrase in OUTCAR.
Ending is not the same as converging.

prompt: A cell relaxation ended after NSW steps with large forces. Is it relaxed?

options.text: No, it stopped for running out of steps
options.why: The criterion was not reached, so the structure is not relaxed.
Tempting, but finishing is not the same as reaching the criterion.
Tempting, but the energy can fall and the forces still be large.

hints: Compare the largest force with EDIFFG.
What stopped the run?

prompt: After a cell relaxation, which energy do you report?

options.text: The static calculation on the relaxed structure
options.why: The relaxation used a basis built for the starting cell, so a static run on the final geometry is the one to report.

options.text: The last energy of the relaxation
options.why: Tempting, but it was computed with the basis of the starting cell.

options.text: The first energy of the relaxation
options.why: Tempting, but that belongs to the starting structure.

hints: What was the basis built for?
Copy CONTCAR to POSCAR and run again.

prompt: Which checks does the handbook suggest after a relaxation?

options.why: Large deviations hint at a wrong magnetic state, missing vdW or a wrong POTCAR.

options.text: Compare the space group of POSCAR and CONTCAR
options.why: Symmetry can be lost during a relaxation.

options.text: Check the number of CPU cores used
options.why: Tempting, but the core count does not tell you whether the structure is right.

hints: One is about the size, one about symmetry.
What would a wrong structure show?

prompt: Why does the handbook use ENCUT of 1.3 times ENMAX for cell relaxations?

options.text: To keep the Pulay stress small
options.why: Stress converges more slowly than energy, so the cutoff needs a margin.
Tempting, but a higher cutoff makes it slower.
Tempting, but ENCUT does not change the functional.

hints: What changes in the basis when the cell changes?
Which quantity converges slowest?

prompt: What does the density of states count?

options.text: The number of electron states per unit energy
options.why: Where the curve is zero there are no states at that energy.

options.text: The number of atoms per unit volume
options.why: Tempting, but that is a density of atoms, not of states.

options.text: The number of electrons in the cell
options.why: Tempting, but that is the integral of the DOS, not the DOS itself.

hints: Read the axes: energy and states per eV.
What happens at an energy with no states?

prompt: The DOS is non-zero at the Fermi level. What does that suggest?

options.text: A metal at this level of theory
options.why: States are available right at the Fermi level, so electrons can move.
Tempting, but an insulator has a gap that contains the Fermi level.
Tempting, but a non-zero DOS at E_F is normal for a metal.

hints: Is there a gap around zero?
Compare with the insulator case.

prompt: Why do you need the POSCAR to group a DOSCAR by element?

options.text: DOSCAR lists atoms by number and does not store element names
options.why: The projected blocks are in atom order only.

options.text: DOSCAR holds only the total DOS
options.why: Tempting, but it can hold projected blocks when LORBIT is set.
Tempting, but the POSCAR holds the structure, not the DOS.

hints: What identifies each projected block?
Which file maps numbers to elements?

prompt: Which tag writes the site- and orbital-projected DOS?

options.why: With LORBIT = 11 the nine orbital columns are written for each atom.
Tempting, but NEDOS is the number of energy points, not a switch for projection.
Tempting, but ISMEAR sets the smearing method.

hints: It starts with L, a logical-like switch.
The tag is named after orbitals.

prompt: Why read a gap from the unsmoothed DOS?

options.text: Smoothing broadens peaks and can fill in a small gap
options.why: It only changes how the curve looks, so it can hide the gap.

options.text: Smoothing is not allowed in VASP
options.why: Tempting, but smoothing is a plotting choice; it is just not physics.

options.text: The unsmoothed DOS has no noise
options.why: Tempting, but it is spiky, but its gaps are the ones in the data.

hints: What does Gaussian broadening do to edges?
Is smoothing physics or presentation?

prompt: What is plotted along the horizontal axis of a band structure?

options.text: Position along a path through the Brillouin zone
options.why: The x axis is the running distance along the k-path, with labelled points.
Tempting, but energy is on the vertical axis.
Tempting, but nothing in a band structure changes with time.

hints: What does each point of the path represent?
Names like Gamma and X label it.

prompt: In route A of the protocol (VASP 6.3 or newer), where does the path go?

options.text: Into a KPOINTS_OPT file next to the uniform mesh in KPOINTS
options.why: VASP then writes the bands on that path from the same job.
Tempting, but POSCAR holds the structure, not the path.
Tempting, but the INCAR holds tags, the path goes into a KPOINTS-style file.

hints: The mesh stays in KPOINTS.
The name ends with _OPT.

prompt: In route B, what does ICHARG = 11 do in the band run?

options.text: It reads the saved CHGCAR and keeps the density fixed
options.why: The bands are then computed on the line-mode path without a new SCF.
Tempting, but it reads one, it does not write one.
Tempting, but that is ISPIN.

hints: The density comes from an earlier run.
Fixed means non-self-consistent.

prompt: Which smearing is not meaningful for the line-mode path run?

options.why: It needs a mesh of at least four points and is not meaningful on a line.
Tempting, but this is the one the workflow uses for the path.
Tempting, but this one works on any set of k-points.

hints: Tetrahedra need a mesh.
Which method divides the zone into tetrahedra?

prompt: Why does a path that misses a band edge give a gap that is too large?

options.text: The true minimum or maximum may lie off the path
options.why: The gap is read only at the k-points in the file.
Tempting, but the functional is fixed in the INCAR.
Tempting, but the bands are the same; only the sampling differs.

hints: Where is the gap read from?
What if an extreme lies between path points?

prompt: The valence band maximum and the conduction band minimum are at the same k-point. The gap is...

options.why: Direct means both extremes sit at the same k.
Tempting, but indirect means they are at different k-points.
Tempting, but a metal has no gap at all.

hints: Compare the two k-points.
Same k means no change of momentum.

prompt: Bands cross the Fermi level on your path. What is reported?

options.text: A metallic system with no gap
options.why: A band holds occupied and empty states, so there is no gap to report.

options.text: A gap of zero for an insulator
options.why: Tempting, but a zero gap here means a metal, not an insulator.
Tempting, but a direct gap needs a gap to exist.

hints: Is there any energy range without states at E_F?
Occupied and empty states in one band.

prompt: Which statement about a PBE band gap is right?

options.why: The handbook uses HSE06 or mBJ for quantitative gaps.
Tempting, but the Kohn-Sham gap is not the optical gap.

options.text: It is always larger than experiment
options.why: Tempting, but semilocal functionals tend to underestimate gaps.

hints: Recall the functional ladder.
Which functionals does the handbook suggest for gaps?

prompt: The VBM is at -0.20 eV and the CBM is at 1.35 eV. What is the band gap?
hints: Gap is CBM minus VBM.
Mind the sign of the VBM.

prompt: What do you divide the CHGCAR numbers by to get electrons per cubic angstrom?

options.why: Each value is the density times the cell volume.
Tempting, but the values are scaled by volume, not by atom count.
Tempting, but that is used for the electron count, not for the density.

hints: Look at the header of CHGCAR.
What is multiplied in?

prompt: Which method turns a grid of density values into a surface?

options.why: It looks at each small cube of the grid and draws the piece of surface that crosses it.
Tempting, but that moves between real and reciprocal space, it does not draw a surface.
Tempting, but that is a k-point mesh.

hints: The surface is built cube by cube.
Lorensen and Cline, 1987.

prompt: How can you check that a CHGCAR belongs to your system?

options.text: Sum the grid values and divide by the number of grid points to get the electron count
options.why: That should equal the valence electrons of the system.

options.text: Count the lines in the file
options.why: Tempting, but the line count depends on the grid and layout, not on the system.
Tempting, but the first line is a free comment.

hints: What does the density integrate to?
Include only valence electrons.

prompt: What does the second grid in a spin-polarized CHGCAR hold?

options.text: The magnetization, spin up minus spin down
options.why: It is the magnetization density in the same layout as the first grid.
Tempting, but core electrons are not written here.

options.text: The density at the next step
options.why: Tempting, but CHGCAR holds one converged density.

hints: ISPIN = 2 adds something.
Which difference is a magnetization?

prompt: You raise the isosurface level. What happens?

options.text: The surface shrinks to enclose only the densest regions
options.why: Only places with a high density stay inside the surface.

options.text: The surface grows and joins atoms
options.why: Tempting, but that is what a lower level does.
Tempting, but the level decides which density value the surface follows.

hints: A high level means a rare value.
Where is the density highest?
